name: MarburgumII User Interface and HUD Ontology
compatibility: Companion semantic layer to Data/Ontology/core.v0.1.json, not a network packet or Unreal blueprint schema.

type_definitions.description: An active local player's interface lifecycle, independent of account identity or server session.
A mutually or partly exclusive context that selects relevant HUD modules, e.g. exploration or driving.
A truthful client connection/join/recovery state, distinguished from renderer loading.
A root screen-space or world-space container with layering, input and visibility contracts.
A stable named interface feature with semantic responsibility and render contract.
The actual active projection of a module for a player and viewport.
A reusable control or content primitive within a module.
A responsive safe-area region in which modules may be anchored or docked.
A saved set of positions, sizes and visibility choices for configurable modules.
Rules for safe area, bounds, collision avoidance, minimum readable size and stacking.
A predicate over context, data availability, player settings and priority.
A typed piece of presentation-relevant state with declared provenance, freshness and privacy.
A client projection that turns signals into display-ready, localizable content.
A user request for a gameplay-affecting action; never itself a successful outcome.
An acknowledged server-owned outcome or rejection keyed to a stable operation ID.
A deduplicated signal of meaningful change shown through visual and optional audio channels.
Priority, queuing, aggregation, persistence and acknowledgement rules for feedback events.
Compact server-derived player condition and identity context.
Information about a selected, addressed or nearby relevant entity, subject to visibility/privacy.
Compact summaries of other party members from authorized session data.
A progress, readiness, duration or state cue for an active noncombat or bounded-danger activity.
One actionable verb, input glyph, target and eligibility feedback at a time.
A pinned concise objective, separate from full mission history.
A transient, period-correct display name for a visited place.
Optional context-sensitive local wayfinding using only approved knowledge and period conventions.
A controlled, readable channel of event and reward messages.
Optional compact actions/tools tied to actual owned capabilities, not a permanent combat hotbar.
The inventory and inspection interface, with quantities, evidence roles and valid actions.
Skill proficiency, earned XP, meaningful unlocks and mastery presentation.
Mission states, objectives, history, evidence and player annotations.
Identity, condition, possessions, authorized equipment and social information.
Focused NPC/player conversation with choices, attribution and server-confirmed results.
Optional party roster, invitations and moderated communication interfaces.
Display, UI scaling, audio, controls, accessibility and recovery settings.
An exclusive confirmation/refusal/error flow with focus and escape semantics.
A semantic command such as interact, open inventory, back or accept.
A layer that owns focus navigation and restore behavior while active.
Versioned typography, color, icon, spacing, sound, border or motion design token.
Culture-aware player-facing text with localization identifier and formatting constraints.
Role/name/description/value/live announcement metadata, not inferred from artwork.
Persisted local appearance, scale, input, contrast and motion settings.
A reproducible target resolution, mode, data state and expected screenshot/interaction outcome.
Labeled deterministic UI preview data that cannot issue authoritative gameplay commands.
A measured CPU/GPU/memory responsiveness expectation for UI surfaces.
Authoritative gameplay availability used to disable/hide unsupported UI actions.

relation_definitions.description: One active session projects a set of UI surfaces.
Modes may overlap subject to precedence rules.
Connection status is an explicit state, not inferred from widget visibility.
Surface owns rendered modules; client instance only.
Stable registered module definition.
Composed reusable controls.
A primary region is assigned per instance.
Safe areas, collision, size and overlay rules.
Visibility policy is explicit, not an ad-hoc Tick check.
Saved local preset determines optional placements.
View models consume typed signals with provenance.
Modules present small view models.
Only supported actions create gameplay intents.
Only the authoritative server resolves consequential intents.
One feed entry may aggregate multiple related events.
Transient versus persistent rules are predictable.
Condition and status originate from authorized signals.
Knowledge-restricted target state only.
Only party-authorized data.
Active work/fishing/vehicle state and duration.
Do not advertise unsupported client-side actions.
Only the pinned currently actionable objective.
Period and fictionalization verified display identity.
Bounded queue/aggregation.
Visual appearance from shared design system.
No hard-coded unlocalizable strings.
Every interactive/essential widget must define semantics.
Visual prompt adapts to currently active input device.
Modal traps focus deliberately and restores prior scope on closing.
UI scale/opacity/language/layout are per-player local choices.
Capture matrix spans modes and data states.
Fixtures are labeled and never claimed as live state.
Profile representative runtime surfaces.
No fake feature completion or actions.
Limited urban activity shortcuts based on real abilities.
Items have only server-supported actions.
Party/social layers obey focus and moderation requirements.

presentation_modes.description: Boot, session/join and recovery interface; no false connected state.
Quiet city exploration with minimal HUD.
Contact or nearby interactable selected, with concise action and contextual subject information.
Evidence inspection, dialogue, mission decisions and journal access.
Fishing, working, photographing, crafting or trading; show only context-specific progress and actions.
Vehicle context; minimal speed, condition if approved, exit action and local navigation.
Small cooperative group; important member state and invitations without default raid-size clutter.
Character, skills, inventory, journal and settings as deliberate large on-demand screens.
Confirmation, refusal, critical network error or destructive action in exclusive focus.

semantic_signals.description: Connection/handshake/timeout lifecycle; 'ready' requires verified actual session.
Server-replicated contract version and compatibility.
Public/owner-visible player identity; avoid account secrets.
Vitality/stamina and condition only if available.
Selected/nearby semantic subject with eligibility and privacy limits.
Actual permitted verbs and verified targets.
Display name with period, map and fictionalization provenance.
Pinned mission and one current actionable objective.
Committed mission progress and evidence reference history.
Committed or rejected mission-related player intent.
Items, validated quantities, status and custody.
Money/explicit currency for client owner only.
Skill level/XP and allowed unlocks.
Current public reputation; contextual private standing is restricted.
Unique XP/item/currency/evidence result, dedupe by transaction/operation identity.
Owned/occupied vehicle identity, speed, condition and authorization.
Active fishing/work/trade state and progression.
Party-visible summary, join/leave state and permitted member condition.
Server-validated, plain-text on-server general message delivered to each owning client via unicast RPC, never global GameState history. Source status: committed C++ not native-tested.
Shared in-world date/time distinct from wall clock.
Meaningful hazard/condition alerts; only when that mechanic exists.
Keyboard/mouse/controller glyph and device-family detection.
Interface scale, opacity, contrast, motion, preference, preset.
Validated module positions/sizes/visibility stored client-side.
Localization keys and culture-aware formats.
Clearly labeled display-only fixture, never produces authoritative events.
Privacy-scoped server-to-owner unicast containing a direct message; visible to sender and intended connected recipient only.

module_registry.description: Full connection/loading/reconnect shell; truthful statuses and recovery.
Concise progress/error and retry state; never fake admission.
Actionable errors and confirmations with preserved focus.
Compact vitality/stamina module, with meaningful absence/unknown state.
Transient district/landmark transition, archive-aware period identity.
Single concise eligible action with device glyph, localized verb, target.
Selective relevant NPC/object nameplate, not a label above every pedestrian.
One brief actionable objective only while pinned.
Deduped priority queue with actionable error persistence.
Small context-specific activity/tool strip; no mandatory combat action bar.
Fishing/trade/work progress and timing when authorized.
Contextual vehicle identity/speed only when operating a vehicle.
Polished identity/condition/stats/equipment; empty states are honest.
Dense icon/proficiency/XP/milestone grid/list with reviewable unlocks.
Graphical item overview with selection/evidence details and legal actions.
Mission progress, historical records, evidence, timeline and pinning.
Readable attributed dialogue and server-backed response choices.
Interface scaling, text, contrast, input and graphics options.
Small-group status with privacy and UI density limits.

Party invitation/session detail, chat where authorized and moderated. Social chat extensions depend on independently approved moderation/account services; general/private text chat is a separate early UI-03 module.
Subtle period-plausible orientation; no always-on satellite/GPS requirement.
Grid/snap/move/scale/visibility with reset, preview and profiles.
Details on demand, not persistent prose.
Optional time on deliberate request or context; not always on.
Important non-excluded hazards only when real gameplay supports them.
Compact general/private messaging panel; private conversation is never a globally replicated display signal.

invariants.rule: UI may display or propose gameplay changes, but cannot author money/items/XP/mission/state outcomes; server receipt and replication are the only live truth.
Preview fixtures are labeled SAMPLE DATA and isolated from live networking and gameplay commands; public runtime evidence must indicate source.
No wanted stars/heat, police chase/pursuit system or legacy generated Talent UI can be registered or made visible.
A gameplay command intent is distinct from a successful receipt; notifications deduplicate by event/operation identity.
No permanent eight-bar ability array or text-wall; semantic priority and visibility policies preserve the center view.
Never show other players' private inventory, balances, secret missions or NPC data that the server has not authorized.
Modal focus traps intentionally; close/back restores prior focus and relevant gameplay input context.
Loading, unknown, disabled, empty, missing-asset and network-error states have explicit graphics and text; never invent values.
Use localizable strings, diacritic-capable fonts, scale/safe-area constraints, readable text and tested input devices.
Screenshot/capture metadata includes engine/version, source SHA, display size, UI scale and live-vs-fixture distinction.
Hidden complex panels are lazy loaded or otherwise verified not to create unnecessary work; prefer event-driven updates.
The default HUD is visually accepted before optional drag-and-drop editor is promoted; editing cannot hide critical error cues.
